items.stem: You switch to a new embedding model for an existing index. What must you do?

options.text: Re-embed the whole corpus with the new model; vectors from different models are not comparable
options.rationale: Correct: embeddings from different models live in different spaces and cannot be mixed.

options.text: Keep the old vectors and add new ones alongside
options.rationale: Mixing vectors from different models produces meaningless comparisons.

options.text: Only re-embed the queries, not the documents
options.rationale: Queries and documents must share the same embedding space.

options.text: Do nothing, since embeddings are universal

items.explanation: Correct: embeddings from different models live in different spaces and cannot be mixed.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO steps improve the reliability of a similarity threshold? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Calibrate the threshold against labelled relevant/irrelevant pairs
options.rationale: Correct: calibration on real data sets a defensible cut-off.

options.text: Normalise vectors so the chosen metric behaves consistently
options.rationale: Correct: normalisation makes cosine similarity comparisons meaningful.

options.text: Pick a round number and never revisit it
options.rationale: An uncalibrated fixed threshold is unreliable.

options.text: Use a different metric for queries than for documents

items.explanation: Correct: calibration on real data sets a defensible cut-off.

items.stem: Retrieval quality is poor even though the model is strong. What is a likely first thing to inspect?

options.text: How documents are chunked and preprocessed before embedding
options.rationale: Correct: poor chunking commonly degrades retrieval regardless of model quality.

options.text: Whether the corpus has enough total pages
options.rationale: Raw size is not the usual cause of poor relevance.

options.text: Whether the vectors are stored as integers
options.rationale: Storage type is not the typical cause here.

options.text: Whether the model name is capitalised correctly
options.rationale: Naming is irrelevant to retrieval quality.

items.explanation: Correct: poor chunking commonly degrades retrieval regardless of model quality.
